findings.title: Foreground re-entry reloads an already loaded basemap

findings.title: Cancelled scene and bearing calculations are not cooperatively cancellable
findings.evidence: produceState uses withContext(Default) around synchronous groups and offsets (114–118). StopMapClustering and StopMarkerLayout loops have no cancellation checks. StopDirections.collectAsync similarly calls synchronous collect (124–126) without checks in long loops.
findings.trigger: Catalogue/bearing keys change while an older scene computation is running, or composition exits during a large calculation.
findings.impact: Superseded CPU work continues until completion; cancellation cannot free worker capacity promptly and replacement computations can contend.
findings.fix: Pass a cheap cancellation checkpoint into long algorithm loops or use suspending wrappers that ensureActive periodically. Keep pure testable kernels as needed.

findings.title: Focus construction scans the full stop catalogue synchronously in composition
findings.evidence: create performs routes.find (40), fallback allStops scans (65,72,84,89), and an unconditional allStops.filter for contextStops (106–108). MainActivity 219–223 calls create directly inside remember during composition on cache invalidation.

findings.title: Pattern matching computes geometric distance for candidates that scoring later discards
findings.evidence: findMatchingPattern computes distanceToPattern for every candidate (149–150), scanning stops and geometry (205–208), before finding maxScore/filtering at 153–157. findMatchingDirection repeats the eager-distance structure at 192–199.

GLM11 corroborates redundant cleanName/normalize passes inside StopClusters.clusterFor; one shared normalization root, not a separate count.

findings.title: Unconditional 10,000-element list concatenation and indexing in updateStops
findings.evidence: val catalogue = if (national.isEmpty()) local else local + national; catalogue to TransitSearch.indexStops(local, national) creates a new full-catalogue list and rebuilds search indices on every stop update. Parent review: updateStops already skips identical source references; remaining cost is full rebuild on changed catalogue inputs.

findings.impact: Spikes memory allocation and CPU consumption rebuilding the entire search index rather than updating incrementally.

findings.title: Synchronous recalculate() loop executing heavy list sorting and filtering on main thread
findings.evidence: recalculate() runs every 5 seconds from observe() and after every state mutation on Dispatchers.Main, performing departures distinctBy and sortedBy, vehicles filtering, and status message resolution.
findings.trigger: Continuous 5-second polling interval and UI interactions while map or favorites are visible.
findings.impact: Consistently consumes main thread time slices every 5 seconds, causing periodic frame hitches even when the user is idle.
findings.fix: Offload list sorting and transformation to Dispatchers.Default, and debounce recalculate to run only when inputs actually change.

findings.title: Repetitive full-catalogue route deduplication and copying in recalculate()
findings.evidence: (stopRoutes + lineCatalogue + emmaRepository.catalogue).distinctBy { it.id } concatenated and deduplicated on Dispatchers.Main every 5 seconds, passing thousands of routes to EmmaParser.routeCatalogue.
findings.trigger: Every execution of recalculate().
findings.impact: Allocates intermediate collections with thousands of TransitRoute objects and triggers unnecessary emmaRoutes StateFlow emissions.
findings.fix: Pre-combine and cache the route catalogue, updating it only when stopRoutes or lineCatalogue actually changes.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: O(N) linear scan with trigonometric Haversine formula on main thread in nearestStop
findings.evidence: nearestStop iterates through all stops (up to 10,000+) calculating distanceMeters (sin, cos, atan2, sqrt) synchronously on Dispatchers.Main on every location update.
findings.trigger: Every GPS location update received in updateLocation.
findings.impact: Performs tens of thousands of trigonometric floating point calculations on the main thread, resulting in severe jank during user movement.
findings.fix: Apply a fast rectangular bounding-box filter (|lat1 - lat2| < delta) before evaluating Haversine, or compute on Dispatchers.Default.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Repetitive O(N) map association and list re-allocation of emmaStops on main thread
findings.evidence: current.emmaStops.associateBy { it.id }.toMutableMap() is executed over thousands of stops in 6 distinct methods (lines 617, 687, 712, 934, 997, 1030) directly inside mutableState.update on the main thread.
findings.trigger: Map area loading, nearby board arrival, vehicle journey arrival, line loading, and place search results.

findings.fix: Maintain stops as a Map<String, TransitStop> internally in the ViewModel and project to List only where necessary.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Full-collection HashMap allocation in FavoriteDepartures.stations for a few IDs
findings.evidence: FavoriteDepartures.stations(ids, stops) calls stops.associateBy { it.id } on the entire collection of stops (8,000+) just to look up a handful of favorite station IDs.
findings.trigger: Favourite IDs or source catalogue changes, guarded by favoriteNetworkStops/favoriteEmmaStops/favoriteSelectionIds; not every countdown tick.

findings.title: Aggressive 5-second nationwide GraphQL vehicle polling
findings.evidence: while (isActive) { if (mapVisible) refreshEmmaData(); delay(5_000) } polls nationwide vehicle positions covering the entire country every 5 seconds.

findings.fix: Increase polling interval to 15-20 seconds or scope the GraphQL query bounding box to the current viewport.

findings.title: Temporary List allocation churn for distinct keys in recalculate()
findings.evidence: rawDepartures.distinctBy { listOf(it.routeId, it.directionId, it.expectedAt) } allocates an ArrayList with 3 items for every departure candidate. GLM8 also found listOf(routeId,directionId,expectedAt) keys in EmmaStopsParser.boardRow/combineBoards; handled under this same root.

findings.fix: Use a custom value class or compute a 64-bit combined hash key instead of allocating a List.

findings.title: Eager SQLite queries and PlanLeg allocations before domination pruning in walks
findings.evidence: walks constructs a PlanLeg, resolves stop/point metadata and copies the legs list before offer performs horizon/Pareto rejection. stop(id) is cached with getOrPut, so SQL is paid only on its first lookup, not every expansion.
findings.trigger: Every footpath exploration step during offline route planning.
findings.impact: Avoidable candidate objects and first-use metadata lookups for dominated paths; no measured latency claim.
findings.fix: Check the full horizon/Pareto state, including walking cost and the existing LabelKey trip/restriction identity, before constructing PlanLeg or presentation points. Preserve the current dominance semantics.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: N+1 SQLite queries for transfer rules inside inner RAPTOR boarding loop
findings.evidence: db.rawQuery("SELECT seconds,forbidden FROM transfers WHERE from_stop=? AND to_stop=?", ...) is executed per candidate boarding stop inside while (boarding.moveToNext()).
findings.trigger: Every candidate trip evaluation during offline timetable planning.
findings.impact: Multiplies SQLite round-trips into hundreds of individual queries, severely slowing down plan computation.
findings.fix: Pre-load transfer rules into an in-memory sparse map before entering the routing rounds.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Redundant intermediate PlanPoint allocation and stop queries during candidate exploration
findings.evidence: intermediate += point(to) allocates a PlanPoint for every evaluated downstream stop, including trips never retained. stop(id) uses a per-plan getOrPut cache; it is not an uncached SQLite query per call.
findings.trigger: Every intermediate stop along evaluated trips in RAPTOR rounds.
findings.impact: Repeated intermediate presentation objects during routing; metadata SQL is cached and not multiplied per repeated stop.
findings.fix: Store intermediate stop IDs as primitive Longs and resolve stop metadata only for the final selected itineraries.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: N+1 child stop queries in resolve(endpoint) on planner startup
findings.evidence: Iterates over source IDs executing SELECT id,station FROM stops followed by SELECT id FROM stops WHERE parent=? AND station=0 sequentially.
findings.trigger: Start of every offline plan query.
findings.impact: Performs multiple sequential database round-trips to resolve platforms before routing starts.
findings.fix: Batch platform resolution into a single query using WHERE source_id IN (...) OR parent IN (...).
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Repeated SQLiteStatement compilation inside loops in importLocal
findings.evidence: db.compileStatement("INSERT INTO ...") is called inside validStops.forEach and for (route in providerRoutes), compiling and closing statements on each iteration.
findings.trigger: Local GTFS / network timetable import.
findings.impact: Forces SQLite to parse SQL and generate VDBE bytecode for every single row instead of reusing a prepared statement.
findings.fix: Compile statement once before the loop, bind values in the loop, and close it in a finally block.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Quadratic O(R * T) trip filtering in importLocal
findings.evidence: for (route in providerRoutes) { for (trip in network.trips.filter { it.routeId == route.id }) ... } scans the entire network.trips collection linearly for each route.
findings.trigger: Local network GTFS import.
findings.impact: Quadratic runtime scaling during import with large trip lists.
findings.fix: Pre-group trips by routeId using val tripsByRoute = network.trips.groupBy { it.routeId }.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Uncompiled execSQL in tight loop for stop_times in importLocal
findings.evidence: db.execSQL("INSERT INTO stop_times VALUES(...)") is executed in a loop over all stop times without compiled SQLite statements.
findings.trigger: Local network GTFS import.
findings.impact: Causes string allocation, statement compilation, and teardown for thousands of stop time records.
findings.fix: Use a compiled SQLiteStatement with bindLong/bindString and executeInsert().
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Uncompiled execSQL statements in pathways import loop
findings.evidence: In rows("pathways.txt"), db.execSQL("INSERT INTO paths VALUES(?,?,?)", arrayOf(a, b, time)) is called for each pathway row without statement compilation.
findings.trigger: GTFS archive pathways.txt import.
findings.impact: Unnecessary string parsing and statement compilation overhead per pathway row.
findings.fix: Use a single compiled SQLiteStatement with parameter bindings.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Individual row deletion queries in loop for invalid trips
findings.evidence: invalidTrips.forEach { db.execSQL("DELETE FROM stop_times WHERE trip=?", arrayOf(it)); db.execSQL("DELETE FROM trips WHERE id=?", arrayOf(it)) }.
findings.trigger: Validation step of GTFS import when invalid trips are detected.
findings.impact: Executes 2 * N separate database statements for N invalid trips instead of batched deletions.
findings.fix: Batch trip IDs into chunks of 500 using DELETE FROM ... WHERE trip IN (...).
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Single-row UPDATE statements inside stop times processing loop
findings.evidence: if ((pickup > 1 || dropoff > 1) && restrictedTrips.add(trip)) db.execSQL("UPDATE trips SET restricted=1 WHERE id=?", arrayOf(trip)).
findings.trigger: Processing stop_times.txt with restricted pickups or dropoffs.
findings.impact: Executes individual UPDATE queries interleaved with bulk stop_times insertions.
findings.fix: Collect restricted trip IDs in a set and run a batched UPDATE after stop_times parsing completes.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Connection open/close churn and global lock serialization in read()
findings.evidence: fun <T> read(block: (SQLiteDatabase, OfflinePackMetadata) -> T): T = synchronized(lock) { SQLiteDatabase.openDatabase(...).use { db -> block(db, meta) } } opens and closes a new DB connection for every query.
findings.trigger: Every offline timetable board query, line detail lookup, and routing request.
findings.impact: Discards SQLite memory page cache, prepared statement cache, and schema cache on every call, while serializing all readers on synchronized(lock).
findings.fix: Maintain a persistent read-only SQLiteDatabase instance and invalidate it only upon pack replacement or deletion.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Uncached disk read, JSON parsing, and regex compilation in metadata()
findings.evidence: metadata() reads active.json, parses JSON, compiles Regex("[a-zA-Z0-9-]+"), and stats the database file on every single call.
findings.trigger: Worker progress emissions, repository state updates, and before every store.read() call.
findings.impact: Causes redundant flash disk I/O and object allocations during pack operations and timetable requests.
findings.fix: Cache parsed OfflinePackMetadata in memory with an invalidation hook, and compile the regex statically.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Repeated createNotificationChannel Binder IPC on every progress update tick
findings.evidence: notification(label) calls manager.createNotificationChannel(NotificationChannel(...)) on every progress tick (every 750ms).
findings.trigger: Every 750ms during multi-minute GTFS downloads and SQLite imports.
findings.impact: Triggers hundreds of synchronous Binder IPC calls to NotificationManagerService in system_server.
findings.fix: Create the NotificationChannel once during worker startup or in Application.onCreate().
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: OkHttpClient instance re-allocation on every download source
findings.evidence: val client = NetworkAccessPolicy.protect(OkHttpClient.Builder().connectTimeout(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS)...build()) is instantiated for every source file in download().
findings.trigger: Downloading each GTFS provider archive in the download loop.
findings.impact: Creates new thread pools, connection pools, and SSLContexts rather than reusing existing connection resources.
findings.fix: Reuse a single configured OkHttpClient instance across all source downloads.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Full table scan of routes in line(appId) instead of indexed lookup
findings.evidence: db.rawQuery("SELECT id,source_id,number,name,mode,color,feed FROM routes", null).use { c -> while (c.moveToNext()) if (routeAppId(c.getString(1)) == appId) ... } scans the entire table.
findings.trigger: User selecting a line to inspect line details in offline mode.
findings.impact: Performs a full linear scan of all routes in SQLite, ignoring the UNIQUE index on source_id.
findings.fix: Convert appId to source_id and execute SELECT ... FROM routes WHERE source_id = ?.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: N+1 SQLite queries for stop times per trip in line(appId)
findings.evidence: Inside while (trips.moveToNext()), db.rawQuery("SELECT ... FROM stop_times s JOIN stops st ON st.id=s.stop WHERE s.trip=? ORDER BY s.seq", arrayOf(trips.getLong(0).toString())) is executed for every trip.
findings.trigger: Opening any line details in offline mode.
findings.impact: Issues dozens of separate SQLite queries for a single line, causing perceptible UI delay when loading line details.
findings.fix: Query all pattern stop times for the route in a single JOIN query grouped by trip.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Regex compilation per row when parsing routes in route(c)
findings.evidence: color = c.getString(5).takeIf { it.matches(Regex("[0-9a-fA-F]{6}")) } compiles a new Regex object for every row in routes table.
findings.trigger: Loading route catalogue or inspecting lines in offline mode.
findings.impact: Compiles thousands of identical Regex patterns during offline catalogue initialization.
findings.fix: Define the hex color Regex as a static constant in companion object.
findings.status: implemented; fixed colour regex compiled once

findings.title: Sequential per-platform SQLite queries in board() instead of batched query
findings.evidence: for (id in ids) executes two separate queries (SELECT id FROM stops WHERE source_id=? and departure JOIN) sequentially for each platform ID.
findings.trigger: Selecting a station with multiple platforms in offline mode.
findings.impact: Executes 2 * N queries sequentially instead of querying all platform IDs with WHERE s.stop IN (...).
findings.fix: Resolve platform IDs in one pass and query departures with a single WHERE s.stop IN (...) clause.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Synchronous SharedPreferences.commit() disk write on calling thread in setOffline()
findings.evidence: context.getSharedPreferences("offline", 0).edit().putBoolean("enabled", enabled).commit() uses synchronous commit() rather than apply().
findings.trigger: User toggling offline mode in UI or ViewModel.
findings.impact: Forces synchronous fsync() and disk write on the calling thread, risking UI stutter when invoked from UI components.
findings.fix: Replace .commit() with .apply().
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Several lazy item feeds omit content types
findings.evidence: RouteBrowserCard omits types on its empty/direction rows and keyed direction/stop feeds; LineBrowser omits types on static header/detail/loading/error/empty rows and its nested LazyRow variants; PlannerScreen omits types on partial/title/source rows and its itinerary feed.
findings.trigger: Scroll route directions/stops, planner results, or a multi-variant pattern row; item work scales with list counts, while conditional single rows appear/disappear.
findings.impact: Those lazy containers lack type metadata for conditional rows and homogeneous feeds, which limits compatible slot reuse.
findings.fix: Give every lazy item a stable contentType; use one constant type for each homogeneous feed.
findings.confidence: Confirmed missing reuse metadata; user-visible magnitude needs measurement.
findings.status: implemented; heterogeneous row types declared

findings.title: Pattern families regrouped on every screen recomposition
findings.evidence: The selected-route path evaluates patterns.groupBy { it.familyKey }.size directly in the composable body to derive sheet height; this grouping is not remembered.
findings.trigger: Any ViaBuszScreen recomposition while a route is selected; work/allocation scales with loaded patterns.
findings.impact: Repeats grouping and temporary collection allocation on the composition path for unrelated screen state changes.
findings.fix: Cache the family count by pattern collection or reuse a precomputed count.
findings.confidence: Confirmed repeated composition work; frame impact needs measurement.
findings.status: implemented; source-keyed family count cache

findings.title: Natural badge sorting retokenizes labels for every comparator call
findings.evidence: naturalCompare constructs a Regex and token lists per call; extractStationLines sorts train and other badges through it at lines 103 and 107.
findings.trigger: Favorite station badge derivation; comparator calls scale with badge count and repeat regex/token allocations.
findings.impact: Repeated regex setup and tokenization during row derivation.
findings.fix: Hoist the regex and prepare tokens once per label before sorting, or use a comparator over cached tokens.
findings.confidence: Confirmed repeated work; magnitude depends on badge counts and needs measurement.
findings.status: partially implemented; regex shared, per-comparison tokenization remains

findings.title: UI helper regexes are recompiled at call sites
findings.evidence: LineComponents constructs Regex inline in railLineColor (lines 39-41), lineColor (59), and LineBadge (96); PlannerScreen EndpointField (543) and FavoritesScreen isTrainRoute (71) also construct fixed Regex patterns inline. These helpers run during repeated row/field composition and color classification.
findings.trigger: Composing or updating relevant badges, planner endpoint fields, and favorite rows; each evaluated branch creates a Regex and matcher, multiplied by calls/items.
findings.impact: Repeated pattern compilation and matcher allocation in UI formatting/classification work.
findings.fix: Hoist fixed patterns to reusable private values or use direct prefix/character checks where equivalent.
findings.confidence: Confirmed repeated compilation; frame impact needs measurement.
findings.status: partially implemented; rail prefix regexes shared; remaining fixed helpers pending

findings.title: Planner clock producer runs when no UI consumes its value
findings.evidence: produceState(Instant.now()) loops forever and writes every 15 seconds. now is consumed by JourneyDetail and itinerary cards, but the producer is created before checking whether a selected trip or result list exists; on the initial map screen it has no consumer.
findings.trigger: Remain on the planner map without a selected itinerary; schedules a state update and PlannerScreen recomposition every 15 seconds.
findings.impact: Periodic invalidation of the map planner UI without a displayed time-dependent value.
findings.fix: Create the clock producer only in a branch displaying stale-time/countdown UI, or stop it when no consumer needs the time.
findings.confidence: Confirmed unused updates on the map branch; downstream frame impact needs measurement.
findings.status: implemented; clock only ticks for results during STARTED lifecycle

findings.title: First stop lookup builds the full index synchronously on the UI path
findings.evidence: UiState.stopsById lazily allocates a HashMap and loops over every network and Emma stop; FavoritesScreen checks state.stopsById while building LazyColumn content and RouteBrowserCard calls state.findStop while composing route rows.
findings.trigger: First stop lookup for a UiState instance; construction is O(total stops) with an entry per stop and can recur when a fresh state instance reaches one of these call sites.
findings.impact: Full-catalog indexing may block composition before a visible row resolves; actual jank and recurrence depend on dataset size and state-snapshot lifetime.
findings.fix: Reuse a lookup index across immutable snapshots or build/publish it off the UI thread before composition needs it.
findings.confidence: Synchronous O(N) construction and UI access are confirmed; jank and recurrence need measurement.
findings.status: mitigated; shared across snapshots; initial source-generation construction remains synchronous

findings.title: Repeated pairwise haversine proximity scans in hybrid planning
findings.evidence: transferPairs (88-89) is an O(k^2) all-pairs StopClusters.distanceMeters scan over `relevant`; connectedStops convergence loop (184-190) executes `stops.filter { stop -> ... reached.any { distance(it.position, stop.position) <= TRANSFER_WALK_METERS } }` per fixed-point iteration — full stops x reached haversine scan, repeated until ids stop growing. No cheap lat/lon prefilter (distance() is full haversine with sin/cos/asin/sqrt).
findings.trigger: Once per HybridTripPlanner.plan request; runs inside the limitedParallelism(1) worker so concurrent plans serialize behind it. Local merged networks contribute hundreds of stops.
findings.impact: Adds measurable CPU to every planning search; walkable-density worst case reaches hundreds of thousands of distance evaluations and inflates planning latency including the RemoteKey-sharing window.
findings.fix: Bucket stop coordinates on ~200m grid cells (or sorted-lat strips with lon window) and test only same/adjacent cells in both loops; share one precomputed neighbor adjacency between connectedStops and transferPairs.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Search index caches keyed only on list identity churn on caller instance recreation
findings.evidence: RouteIndex/cachedRoutes (85-103), StopIndex/cachedStops (152-173), VehicleIndex/cachedVehicles (176-196) guard with `source === cached.source` only. Verified callers recreate list instances per refresh: TransitViewModel:523 builds a new emmaRoutes via EmmaParser.routeCatalogue each publish, 858-871 rebuild emmaStops per index publish, refreshData (15s) makes new vehicle lists; PlannerViewModel.updateStops (70-85) re-indexes per instance change. Every miss re-runs normalize() over each route/vehicle and StopClusters.consolidateForSearch over the combined local+nationwide stop list plus per-entry text building (166, words split at 16).
findings.trigger: Every refresh publish (recalculate up to 5s, EMMA feed 5s, local refresh 15s) while CategorizedSearch or the planner stop index is active.
findings.impact: Repeated full re-normalization and nationwide re-consolidation several times per minute during a session; the heaviest data-layer index operation runs redundantly.
findings.fix: Reuse immutable catalogue references across state copies; version the full relevant content when data changes. An IDs-only fingerprint is unsafe because names, modes, aliases and providers affect search. Reuse implemented for UiState; audit remaining caller list reconstruction before adding caches.
findings.status: partially mitigated by shared UiState catalogue generations; remaining real source changes still rebuild indexes

findings.title: setOf literals allocated per row/iteration in hot loops (feed parse, boards, plan parse, calendar predicates)
findings.evidence: Grouped sites, by hotness: EmmaParser.kt:50 mode in setOf('BUS','COACH') per candidate row of parse(); :101 vehicle.providerId in setOf('hev','mav') per vehicle in localVehicles. EmmaStopsParser.kt:63 provider setOf in route() per route row. EmmaJourneyParser.kt:85 realtimeState !in setOf('SCHEDULED','CANCELED') per stoptime row. StopBoardScope.kt:23-24 setOf twice per call, invoked twice per departure row in boardRow (EmmaStopsParser.kt:177,181; up to ~300 rows x 6-stop batches). TripPlanner.kt:121 12-mode setOf per leg per itinerary parse (<=12 itineraries x <=40 legs per plan). ServiceCalendar.kt:35 and HommCalendar.kt:17 weekend setOf per call (per boarding per board tick). TransitSearch.kt:80 provider setOf per token per keystroke in query(); :91 per route at index build. StopClusters.kt:157 provider setOf per cluster member at index build. Each allocates a LinkedHashSet (or vararg singleton) in per-row/tick/keystroke/index-rebuild code (amplified by the identity-keyed-index-cache finding).
findings.trigger: Nationwide feed parse every 5s foreground tick (TransitViewModel.refreshEmmaData, observe 182-186; EmmaFeedClient cache TTL 1s); boards/batches per 20s refresh + user actions; plan and journey parse per search; keystroke queries; index-build sites one-shot.
findings.impact: Constant allocation churn in the hottest parse/query paths; individually small, collectively non-trivial GC pressure during foreground use.
findings.fix: Hoist each literal to a top-level/companion val (e.g. BUS_MODES, LOCAL_PROVIDER_MODES, REALTIME_HANDLED, WEEKEND) or explicit == chains; behavior identical, no new APIs needed.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Regex and DateTimeFormatter compiled per call in hot parse paths
findings.evidence: Per-call compilation: RailSupport.number (16), isTrainDeparture (26), canonicalBadge (36; invoked per departure via BoardingSelection.matches at EmmaRouteParser.kt:40); EmmaParser.parse per colored row (70); EmmaStopsParser.route per route row (69); EmmaJourneyParser.formatTime per stoptime (117, DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern); TripPlanner.variables per plan/walking-batch call (106); GitHubUpdates.parse per release row (22, 29).
findings.trigger: Per row per refresh (feed 5s; boards 20s plus 6-stop batches), per plan request, per opened vehicle journey, per OTA check.
findings.impact: Avoidable Pattern.compile cost and garbage in the hottest parse paths; rail badges and stop-board route parsing are the hot sites.
findings.fix: Promote each pattern/formatter to a private val at file/object level. Behavior identical; no new APIs needed.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Per-boarding recomputation of date-invariant calendar results inside the departures loop
findings.evidence: Inside `index.boardings[selectedId].orEmpty().mapNotNull { ... }` the loop re-evaluates, per boarding, provider-scoped activeCalendar (HommCalendar.activeCalendar(today) 47, KanyargoCalendar 48, ServiceCalendar.isConfirmedWorkingDay 49, ViabuszTimetableParser.activeCalendar 50) although `today` is loop-invariant; `startOfDay.plusMinutes(boarding.minute)` (54) builds a ZonedDateTime per boarding.
findings.trigger: recalculate() every 5s foreground (TransitViewModel observe 176-180) per visible board; StationTimetableRepository.downloadStationTimetable calls departures() per platform with 1440-minute window (263); favorites/nearby too. Hubs have dozens-to-hundreds of boardings.
findings.impact: Repeated date math and allocations x boardings x 5s; at hubs the dominant per-tick data cost besides the TransitSearch index churn.
findings.fix: Cache calendar verdicts lazily per calendar kind within one departures call, including null verdicts. Preserve existing timezone conversion and DST behavior; arithmetic epoch conversion is not part of this fix.
findings.status: implemented: per-call calendar memoization; timezone conversion preserved

findings.title: Holiday set and weekend set rebuilt on every isConfirmedWorkingDay call
findings.evidence: publicHolidays(year) maps 8 fixed MonthDays into a set plus the easter-derived setOf — allocated per call (24-29) including the easter computus; isConfirmedWorkingDay (34) calls it every time and allocates `setOf(DayOfWeek.SATURDAY, DayOfWeek.SUNDAY)` per call (35); HommCalendar.activeCalendar calls isConfirmedWorkingDay again per invocation (HommCalendar.kt:18).
findings.trigger: Per boarding per 5s board tick via calendars; also checkedDate per load path (TransitRepository 130-147).
findings.impact: Identical result recomputed many times per second; trivially memoizable per date/year.
findings.fix: Memoize publicHolidays and working-day verdict keyed by year/date, or compute the per-date boolean once per departures() call alongside the DepartureCalculator hoist.
findings.status: implemented: holiday sets retained only for explicitly reviewed years; weekend membership uses direct comparisons; arbitrary publicHolidays calls remain uncached

findings.title: boardRow re-parses identical route JSON per departure row and re-fetches stops.single() twice per row
findings.evidence: Inside the per-row mapNotNull loop (169-205): `trip.optJSONObject("route")?.let(::route)` (175) runs EmmaStopsParser.route — re-reading mode/short/long names and re-running HevSupport/RailSupport plus the per-call hex Regex (69) — for every row although the route JSON is shared across rows of a pattern; `catalogue.stops.single()` re-evaluated at 176 and 180 within the loop though loop-invariant; StopBoardScope checks (177-181) consume those hoistable values.
findings.trigger: board() per 20s board tick (observe 200-204), batch() for 6-stop clusters, 24h boards per platform during StationTimetableRepository.downloadStationTimetable, servingLines merges.
findings.impact: Duplicated parse work proportional to rows x boards per refresh cycle; with 6-board batches the largest per-tick parser cost in data/.
findings.fix: Cache parsed routes by route gtfsId before the loop (parse is deterministic per row); hoist `val selectedStop = catalogue.stops.single()` and stopMode out of the loop.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: estimate() re-filters all trips per road and re-projects per call; project() recomputes cos(lat) per edge
findings.evidence: Inside the geometry loop: `trips.filter { it.routeId == road.routeId && it.directionId == road.directionId && it.stopTimes.map { t -> t.stopId } == road.stopIds }` (127) re-filters the whole trips list and allocates a stopId list per trip per road per call; `projections = samples.map { edges.map { project(sample.position,it) ... } }` (124-125) recomputed per estimate(); project() (164-173) computes `cos(Math.toRadians(p.lat))` per (sample x edge) though the sample is constant across edges.
findings.trigger: Per qualifying vehicle track (sum>=3 samples, moving, non-terminal, non-stationary) per refresh publish; update() called once per feed refresh (class contract lines 29-31; constructed once per app run TransitViewModel:59).
findings.impact: Moderate per refresh; scales with GPX geometry edge count across the 5 ViaBusz roads.
findings.fix: Precompute `tripsByRoadKey: Map(routeId+directionId -> List<ScheduledTrip>)` with precomputed stopIds at first update; hoist cos(lat) per sample; optionally memoize projections by sample observedAt.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Terminal-stop scan recomputed per vehicle instead of once per update
findings.evidence: `terminal = network.stops.any { stop -> routes.values.any { route -> route.directions.any { it.stopIds.firstOrNull() == stop.id || it.stopIds.lastOrNull() == stop.id } } && distance(stop.position, vehicle.position) < 100 }` (102-105) runs inside `vehicles.map` — per vehicle per refresh — although the terminal-stop set derives only from loop-invariant routes/network.
findings.trigger: Per viaBusz vehicle per refresh publish (15s tick and recalculate events); merged network stop lists are in the hundreds.
findings.impact: Moderate repeated scan per refresh; trivially hoistable.
findings.fix: Compute the terminal stop id set (plus optional proximity index) once at the top of update() and test membership per vehicle.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Bundled-asset decode runs synchronously in init paths on the main thread
findings.evidence: TransitViewModel constructs initialNetwork using repository.bundledNetwork(), which synchronously decodes three assets and merges them. EmmaRepository construction also decodes volan-routes.json. Correction: routeEstimator is lazy and first accessed inside Dispatchers.Default in refreshData, so its geometry decode is excluded from this startup finding.
findings.trigger: Once per app start / first VM creation; blocking work before the first frame.
findings.impact: App-start main-thread jank; cost = asset sizes + SharedStops.merge pass (see the merge-copies finding).
findings.fix: Expose suspend/IO-backed variants (task or withContext-loaded holder published to state) for cold-start paths; keep the pure decode functions for tests.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: resolve() linear scans mapped over every arrival on the hot refresh path
findings.evidence: resolve (17-19) performs `network.stops.firstOrNull { it.id == sourceId }` then `firstOrNull { sourceId in it.sourceStopIds }` — O(stops) + O(sum sourceStopIds) per call. Verified hot caller: TransitViewModel:527 resolves every arrival of the live snapshot per board publish (provider aggregate + per-vehicle arrivals lists), executed on the recalculate cadence (<= 5s); also :982/:1117 per user selection (bounded).
findings.trigger: O(arrivals x stops) per recalculate tick while a stop board is open; arrivals in the hundreds, merged local network stops in the hundreds.
findings.impact: Redundant re-resolution of unchanged stop ids every tick with full scans on the publish path.
findings.fix: Expose DepartureIndex.stopIds (DepartureCalculator.kt:11-15 already builds canonical sourceId->stop.id mapping) for package use, or add a sourceIdIndex map to SharedStops.merge output; resolve once per distinct arrival stop id per refresh.
findings.status: implemented: snapshot-local lazy alias index shared with DepartureIndex, independent of boarding-index construction; exact ID and first-alias precedence tested

findings.title: merge() unconditionally copies all route directions and every StopTime
findings.evidence: direction.stopIds.map(::canonicalId) (32-34) and every trip's StopTime copy (35-37) run although canonicalId is identity for all but 6 alias ids (9-13). Merge executes on every loadNetwork refresh, every planningNetwork (per plan — PlannerViewModel passes TransitRepository::planningNetwork with no memoization, PlannerViewModel.kt:38), and bundledNetwork at startup.
findings.trigger: Per network load and per planner query; thousands of StopTime copies per merge in the merged local network.
findings.impact: Allocation churn contributing to plan-request latency (each HybridTripPlanner.plan awaits a fresh merge).
findings.fix: Skip copy (return the original list/object) when canonicalId leaves the input unchanged; or memoize merge output keyed on source network identity in NetworkMerger.
findings.status: partially implemented: unaffected routes, directions, trips and StopTimes reused; stop metadata and outer list copies remain; exact parity verified

findings.title: Router initialization repeatedly converts stop times and allocates intermediate time lists
findings.evidence: LocalTimetableRouter init builds a nullable times list for every trip across candidate dates, checks it, then allocates filterNotNull output and per-stop boarding lists. Instant comparisons are object comparisons, not primitive boxing; times.any does not allocate another list.
findings.trigger: Constructed once per hybrid plan (HybridTripPlanner.kt:100) on the limitedParallelism(1) worker; also offline planner paths.
findings.impact: Per-plan construction cost adds to planning latency; repeated identical work per plan for an unchanged network snapshot.
findings.fix: Profile constructor cost on representative networks; consider caching fully keyed immutable service-day boarding lists or eliminating redundant intermediate lists. Preserve invalid/ambiguous local-time rejection on DST transitions; do not substitute naive midnight-plus-seconds arithmetic.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Offline board projection re-derives zone times per departure per offline refresh tick
findings.evidence: buildOfflineBoard projection branch (319-331): when nothing is in-window, every stored departure row is converted via `dep.expectedAt.atZone(budapestZone).toLocalTime().toSecondOfDay()` and `dep.copy(...)` then sorted — per getOfflineBoard call. Offline mode recalculates on the same 5s loop (TransitViewModel observe 176-180; recalculateOffline paths 273/432/648; getOfflineBoard 289-297). Station packs store all platforms for a 24h horizon (class doc 49-53) — potentially hundreds-to-thousands of rows.
findings.trigger: Per 5s tick in offline mode per offline station view.
findings.impact: Moderate; repeated identical zone conversions per tick for unchanged data.
findings.fix: Precompute secondOfDay per departure once when the timetable loads (field on StationTimetable) or index departures by minute-of-day; the tick projection becomes lookup-only.
findings.status: open; source cost identified, runtime benefit unmeasured

findings.title: servingLines memory cache evicts by insertion order, not recency
findings.evidence: `lineMemory = linkedMapOf<String, Lines>()` (72) is insertion-order; hit path (81) and overwrite (88) never reorder; eviction `while (lineMemory.size>64) lineMemory.remove(lineMemory.keys.first())` (89) removes oldest-inserted. Contrast StationTimetableRepository which uses access-order (LinkedHashMap(8, 0.75f, true), line 62) correctly.
findings.trigger: Every servingLines call past 64 distinct stations per session.
findings.impact: Bounded — evicted entries fall back to the daily disk cache (81-82), so cost is an extra file decode; eviction order is still wrong and wastes warm entries.
findings.fix: Use LinkedHashMap(16, 0.75f, true) with removeEldestEntry, matching the other LRU sites.
findings.status: implemented: access-order bounded 64-entry map; disk hits promoted into memory, still protected by the existing mutex

findings.title: Historical process-exit retrieval and crash-file work run synchronously during Application startup
findings.evidence: Application.onCreate invokes ActivityManager.getHistoricalProcessExitReasons before activity creation; when a recent relevant exit exists it also reads/writes last-crash.txt and preferences synchronously. Moving the later Compose crash read to IO does not remove this earlier work.
findings.trigger: Every API30+ process startup for the history query; file work only for a newly discovered relevant exit.
findings.impact: Binder latency on the cold-start critical path, plus conditional storage work before the activity can draw; duration unmeasured.
findings.fix: Install the uncaught-exception handler synchronously, then fetch historical exits on IO. Coordinate report publication with the activity so delayed reports are shown and a newer Java report cannot be overwritten.
findings.confidence: confirmed synchronous call path; startup impact needs device measurement
findings.status: open; preserve crash-report ordering before changing startup execution

findings.title: Selected-platform lookup scans the whole catalogue after every UiState copy
findings.evidence: StopBoardScope.platforms builds the selected-ID set, then calls stops.filter { it.id in ids }.distinctBy { it.id }. UiState.selectedPlatforms is lazy per UiState instance, so recalculate reading it after a clock/state copy rescans the shared catalogue even when selection and catalogue sources are unchanged.
findings.trigger: Departure-board refreshes and other state copies while a stop is selected; catalogue can include national stops.
findings.impact: O(catalogue size) work to retrieve a few explicitly selected platforms. Sharing catalogue lists/maps does not itself reuse this derived selection.
findings.fix: Cache selected-platform results by catalogue identity and selected IDs, or maintain a first-encounter index with catalogue order. Preserve current first-duplicate and encounter-order behavior; UiState.stopsById has different national-over-local precedence and is not a drop-in replacement.
findings.confidence: source path confirmed; runtime impact unmeasured
findings.status: open; prioritize using representative release traces

findings.title: Offline lookup predicates lack parent-stop and route-trip indexes
findings.evidence: Schema indexes cover boarding, trip service, service date, transfers, paths and stop search, but not stops(parent) or trips(route). OfflineTripPlanner resolves station children with WHERE parent=? AND station=0; OfflineTransitData.line loads trips with WHERE route=?. Existing UNIQUE(source_id) and INTEGER PRIMARY KEY indexes cannot service those predicates.
findings.trigger: Station endpoint expansion and offline line detail loading on installed national packs.
findings.impact: Scans national stop/trip tables even when only one station or route is requested. Distinct from batching child queries or fixing the routes(source_id) lookup.
findings.fix: Use EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN against representative packs; add suitable stops(parent,station) and trips(route) indexes during pack construction, with an explicit policy for already-installed packs.
findings.confidence: source path confirmed; runtime impact unmeasured
findings.status: open; prioritize using representative release traces

findings.title: Offline boards read and convert four service days before filtering a short window
findings.evidence: The departure JOIN restricts service days but not departure seconds. Every matching row for day-2 through day+1 is converted via serviceInstant, then checked against now/until in Kotlin. Only after full collection/sort is take(300) applied.
findings.trigger: Each offline board refresh, including 30-minute boards at busy stops.
findings.impact: Reads, timezone-converts and sorts out-of-window rows. This remains even if the per-platform queries from Gemini38 are batched.
findings.fix: Compute service-base instants once per candidate day, then pass safe per-day departure-second bounds to SQL using the existing boarding index. Preserve extended GTFS times, DST noon-origin semantics and final global ordering/limit.
findings.confidence: source path confirmed; runtime impact unmeasured
findings.status: open; prioritize using representative release traces

findings.title: Routing repeatedly queries the same downstream stop-time sequences
findings.evidence: Inside each boarding candidate, SELECT stop,arrival,dropoff FROM stop_times WHERE trip=? AND seq>? ORDER BY seq executes again. Different Pareto labels and rounds can board the same trip/sequence; only stop/route metadata is currently cached.
findings.trigger: Offline searches with alternative access paths or multiple labels reaching the same boarding stop.
findings.impact: Repeated SQLite cursor setup and reads for invariant trip sequences. Separate from transfer-rule queries and intermediate PlanPoint allocation.
findings.fix: Cache one immutable stop-time sequence per encountered trip within a planning invocation and select its seq suffix without another SQL query. Bound cache lifetime to that invocation and preserve drop-off restrictions and overtaking trips.
findings.confidence: source path confirmed; runtime impact unmeasured
findings.status: open; prioritize using representative release traces

findings.title: Opened line geometries remain in an unbounded session cache
findings.evidence: lineLoadedAt[id] records timestamps and UiState.lineDetails is updated using current.lineDetails + (id to details). Neither path evicts old IDs; the 600-second freshness check only controls refetching. Cached LineDetails retain every pattern stop and geometry.
findings.trigger: Browsing many different national routes in a long session.
findings.impact: Retained memory and map copying grow with distinct opened routes. Sol18 covers bearing rebuild CPU; this is the independent cache-retention root.
findings.fix: Introduce a bounded cache with explicit retention of the currently selected/tracked routes. Publish only required details to UI and evict paired freshness entries. Measure retained heap before choosing a bound.
findings.confidence: source path confirmed; runtime impact unmeasured
findings.status: open; prioritize using representative release traces

findings.title: Blocking provider and OTA HTTP calls outlive coroutine cancellation
findings.evidence: TransitRepository.execute uses client.newCall(request).execute().use without a cancellation hook. OtaRepository.fetchUpdateInfo and downloadApk also execute blocking calls; download checks ensureActive between chunks but cannot cancel a blocked header/body read.
findings.trigger: Cancelling refresh/OTA jobs, switching channels, leaving screens, or clearing the ViewModel while a server stalls. NetworkAccessPolicy cancels all clients only on entering offline mode, which does not cover ordinary job cancellation.
findings.impact: Unused sockets, bandwidth and IO-worker occupancy can continue until the blocking read finishes or a timeout fires.
findings.fix: Bridge OkHttp enqueue through suspendCancellableCoroutine with invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() }, keeping streaming body consumption cancellation-aware and preserving temporary-file cleanup. Test cancellation while headers and body reads are stalled.
findings.confidence: source path confirmed; runtime impact unmeasured
findings.status: open; prioritize using representative release traces

findings.title: One serving-line mutex serializes unrelated station requests
findings.evidence: servingLines holds linesMutex.withLock across disk read, graphql.execute, parsing and disk write. The favourites loader launches up to three concurrent requests under a semaphore, but this repository lock permits only one station request to progress.
findings.trigger: Opening several uncached favourite stations; a slow miss also blocks memory hits for other stations.
findings.impact: Head-of-line latency across independent stations; the configured favourites concurrency cannot be used.
findings.fix: Keep map access/eviction atomic under a short lock and coalesce in-flight requests per stop ID. Permit bounded parallel I/O for different IDs, preserve force semantics and atomic cache-file replacement.
findings.confidence: source path confirmed; runtime impact unmeasured
findings.status: open; prioritize using representative release traces

rejectedOrMerged.title: Deep structural collection equality checking in LaunchedEffect for emmaStops
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: LaunchedEffect(tab, state.network?.stops, state.emmaStops) { if (tab == MainTab.PLANNER) planner.updateStops(...) }. Because stability_config.conf marks List as stable, Compose evaluates structural .equals() across up to 10,000 stops on each recomposition.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Every recomposition of MainActivity content when emmaStops reference changes.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Stalls the main thread traversing thousands of TransitStop elements to verify equality, dropping UI frames.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Key the LaunchedEffect on a generation counter, revision number, or collection size rather than the complete list instance.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: No demonstrated fresh, deeply equal hot inputs; List.equals short-circuits identical references.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Frequent nationwide stop bearing recalculation triggered by vehicle updates
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: produceState keys include state.vehicleJourney and state.emmaRoutes: value = StopDirections.collectAsync(state.routes, state.stops, state.lineDetails.values, state.vehicleJourney). Whenever live vehicle positions refresh, full network bearings recompute.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Vehicle feed updates every 5 to 15 seconds.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Continuous background coroutine CPU churn and map layer re-draws for stops across the entire country.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Restrict stop bearing calculation only to active line focus stops or viewport-visible stops, and decouple keys from live vehicle jitter.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Expensive structural equality checks on large collections in LineMapFocus remember keys
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: remember(vehicle?.id, vehicle?.routeId, boarding, state.network, state.emmaRoutes, state.lineDetails, state.vehicleJourney, state.emmaStops) passes large collections (emmaRoutes, lineDetails, emmaStops) as remember keys.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Any recomposition of the map container in ViaBuszScreen content slot.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Evaluates structural equals across thousands of stops and routes on every recomposition pass.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Key remember only on lightweight identity primitives such as vehicle?.id, boarding?.routeId, and a lineDetails revision epoch.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: No demonstrated repeated deep traversal; remember equality does not imply every catalogue is traversed.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Unmemoized Color.toArgb() conversion during composition in map slot
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: routeColor = color.toArgb() in NativeTransitMap invocation inside ViaBuszScreen content slot is evaluated on every recomposition frame without remember.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Every recomposition while displaying an active route or vehicle.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Redundant color conversion calculations and argument churn during map animation frames.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Wrap routeColor calculation in remember(color) { color.toArgb() } or pass Color directly to the native bridge.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: Color.toArgb is a trivial conversion; memoization is not a supported performance fix.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Synchronous LocationManagerCompat Binder IPC in UI click listener
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: onLocate callback executes val manager = getSystemService(Context.LOCATION_SERVICE) as LocationManager; if (!LocationManagerCompat.isLocationEnabled(manager)) synchronously on the main thread.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: User tapping the locate button in ViaBuszScreen.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Synchronous Binder IPC call to LocationManagerService on button tap induces micro-stutter before showing feedback.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Cache location service enabled status via BroadcastReceiver or query asynchronously.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: Merged into startup/system-service IPC review (Gemini6); do not count a second generic IPC root.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Repeated flatMap and distinct allocations during endpoint cluster consolidation
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: cluster.flatMap { it.sourceStopIds }.distinct(), cluster.flatMap { it.providerIds }.distinct(), and cluster.flatMap { it.routeIds }.distinct() allocate numerous intermediate lists and iterators for every clustered hub.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Every execution of consolidateEndpoints during station search.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: High GC allocation rate and memory pressure on the main thread during typing.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Accumulate IDs into reusable LinkedHashSets in a single traversal of the cluster.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: Bounded search result clustering; small collection allocations alone are not established bottlenecks.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Redundant disk read and JSON parse of offline pack metadata on network policy changes
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: val metadata = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { offlineStore.metadata() } runs inside NetworkAccessPolicy.offline.collect on every connectivity transition.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Any network state change between online and offline.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Triggers disk file read of active.json, JSON parsing, and regex validation despite metadata already being cached in memory.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Read cached metadata from OfflinePackRepository instead of hitting disk via offlineStore.metadata().
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: Already IO dispatched and policy transitions are not every connectivity callback; metadata cost covered by Gemini32.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Uncached single-row SQLite queries in stop(id) and route(id)
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: stop(id) and route(id) call db.rawQuery("SELECT ... WHERE id=?") on every invocation without in-memory query caching.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Repeated stop and route lookups during RAPTOR routing.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Repeatedly executes identical SQLite queries for common junction stops and routes.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Introduce a local LongSparseArray cache for stops and routes during the routing session.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: False positive: stop(id) and route(id) explicitly use getOrPut caches.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Uninterned String allocations for repeated fields in CSV parsing
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: field.toString() allocates a new String instance for every column of every row in stop_times.txt across millions of records.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Parsing large GTFS CSV files (stop_times.txt, trips.txt).
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Generates hundreds of megabytes of short-lived String allocations, triggering frequent garbage collection pauses.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Use a bounded string cache / intern table for high-cardinality repetitive identifiers, or parse numeric IDs directly.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: Parsing requires field strings; indiscriminate interning is not justified and could retain unbounded inputs.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Ephemeral native thread and dispatcher creation per offline database invocation
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor { Thread(task, "OfflinePackDatabase") }.asCoroutineDispatcher().use { ... } spawns and destroys an OS thread and dispatcher on each call.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Any invocation of onOfflineDatabaseThread during pack import or maintenance.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Incurs native thread creation and stack allocation overhead (~1MB virtual memory) for transient blocks.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Maintain a single long-lived single-thread executor dispatcher for offline database operations.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: Dedicated per-import thread is intentional transaction/thread-affinity protection; no measured material setup cost.

rejectedOrMerged.title: distinctBy key allocates a 3-element List per departure row
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: `.distinctBy { listOf(it.routeId, it.directionId, it.expectedAt) }` at 205 (boardRow result) and again on merged boards in combineBoards (230) — ArrayList + array backer allocated per row of the dedupe key on full board results (up to BOARD_LIMIT rows plus multi-board merges), every refresh.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Small; GC noise in the board path.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Key with a Triple<String,String,Instant> (single object) or a value-class composite stored on Departure.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: Merged into Gemini18: the same temporary List deduplication-key root also occurs in EmmaStopsParser.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Cluster name matching re-normalizes strings already cleaned by callers; normalize() always runs NFD
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: clusterFor (90-107) computes cleanTargetName (91) and cleanOtherName (101) then calls areNamesCloselyMatching(target.name, other.name) (102), which re-runs normalize() and cleanName() on both raw names (51-57): up to 4 normalize + 4 cleanName passes per near candidate. StopClusters.normalize (24-28) has no ASCII fast path (unlike TransitSearch.normalize 49-65); cleanName chains 6 regex replaces (30-39). consolidateForSearch (118 groupBy cleanName) scales this over the combined national index at every index rebuild.
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: consolidateForSearch per indexStops rebuild (frequency per TransitSearch cache churn); clusterFor on stop-share/download flows (TransitViewModel:1178 per download tap; isMultiStop API currently has no production caller).
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Worst combined with index rebuilds; elsewhere user-action bounded. Pure redundant work in the close-match path.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: ASCII fast path in normalize() mirroring TransitSearch; overload areNamesCloselyMatching for pre-cleaned inputs used by clusterFor.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: Merged into Sol22: repeated stop-name cleaning/normalization in shared matching utilities.

rejectedOrMerged.title: Hub word scan computed for every index entry before the term filter
rejectedOrMerged.evidence: Per index entry, line 17 runs `hubs.firstOrNull { key -> entry.words.any { it.startsWith(key) } }` (4 hub keys x every entry word) BEFORE the term loop that can reject the entry (20-29); hub is only needed for scoring matched entries (30-31) and the generic bonus. Runs per keystroke over the shared stop index (CategorizedSearch.kt:73-74; PlannerViewModel.kt:222-223).
rejectedOrMerged.trigger: Per keystroke over local+nationwide stop index.
rejectedOrMerged.impact: Moderate input amplification on search-as-you-type CPU; highest when the index spans the national catalogue.
rejectedOrMerged.fix: Move hub computation after the term-match short-circuit; compute lazily only for entries that matched at least one term.
rejectedOrMerged.rejectionReason: Rejected proposed reordering: hub is read inside the station-word matching branch, before scoring. Moving it below term matching changes semantics.
